record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: What is the topological type of the achievement set E(x_n) when x_{2n-1} = 1/2^{2n-1} and x_{2n} = 1/(2^{2n}+1)?

evidence.quote: What is the topological type of E(xn) for x2n−1 := 1/2^(2n−1) and x2n := 1/(2^(2n)+1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an absolutely summable sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive real numbers, define the achievement set
$$E(x_n) := \left\{\sum_{n\in A} x_n : A\subseteq \mathbb{N}\right\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}.$$
Consider the specific sequence given by
$$x_{2n-1} := \frac{1}{2^{2n-1}}, \qquad x_{2n} := \frac{1}{2^{2n}+1}, \qquad n=1,2,3,\dots$$
Determine the topological type of the achievement set $E(x_n)$. In particular, decide whether $E(x_n)$ is homeomorphic to a finite union of closed intervals, to a Cantor set, to a Cantorval (i.e., a nonempty compact set in $\mathbb{R}$ that is the closure of its interior, has no isolated points, and whose complement in its convex hull is dense), or to some other topological type.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets (2026). It is related to broader open questions on classifying topological types of achievement sets of series whose center-set K(x_n) consists of even or odd indices, connected to the Second Jones Problem. No solution appears in the current literature.
